title: Impact of maternal fasting blood glucose in pregnancy on body composition, anthropometric, and metabolic outcomes in newborns and 3-Year-Old offspring: results from the lifestyle in pregnancy and offspring study.
ehr_evidence: The analysis used data from the Lifestyle in Pregnancy (LiP) study and its 3-year follow-up, the LiPO study (a randomised controlled trial of lifestyle intervention in obese pregnant women and its prospective follow-up with DXA, anthropometric, and blood measurements).
summary: A secondary analysis of the LiP randomised controlled trial and its 3-year LiPO follow-up in obese Danish pregnant women examined whether maternal fasting plasma glucose at 28 weeks predicts offspring birth weight/anthropometric and metabolic outcomes at birth and at 3 years.
key_findings: Higher maternal fasting plasma glucose at GA 28 was associated with a significantly higher birth weight z-score (β = 0.48, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.75, p = 0.001).
Maternal fasting glucose was not significantly associated with birth weight in grams (β = 103 g, 95% CI −43 to 249, p = 0.167).
At 3 years, no significant associations were found between maternal fasting glucose and BMI z-score or any cardiometabolic markers.
Non-significant trends toward greater adiposity at 3 years: total fat mass (β = 160 g, 95% CI −0.30 to 0.62, p = 0.495) and fat-free mass (β = 262 g, 95% CI −623 to 1149, p = 0.167).
No significant effect modification by breastfeeding duration was observed for any 3-year outcome.
Newborns of women meeting the WHO2013 GDM criterion had higher birth weight z-scores (0.474 vs. 0.135, p = 0.01).
Maternal fasting glucose ≥ 5.6 mmol/L predicted a significantly higher proportion of large-for-gestational-age infants.
Maternal fasting glucose ≥ 5.3 mmol/L predicted higher cord c-peptide (592 pmol/L vs. 430 pmol/L, p = 0.01).
captured_features: Maternal fasting plasma glucose at GA 28 (mmol/L)
study_design: Secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial (LiP) with a prospective 3-year follow-up (LiPO)
population: Obese pregnant women (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) from Odense and Aarhus University Hospitals, Denmark; 301 in LiP, 157 in LiPO follow-up, 75 children with DXA; offspring assessed at birth and at ~3 years
exposure_domain: Maternal fasting blood glucose in pregnancy (metabolic/glucose homeostasis)
limitations: Low ~50% follow-up participation at the 3-year assessment.
Missing DXA data due to inadequate scan quality in young children.
Small subgroup sample sizes limiting statistical power and increasing type II error risk.
data_availability_statement: The data that support the findings of this study are available from C.A.V., but restrictions apply to their availability. The data were used under license for the current study and include unpublished results that are still being analyzed. Therefore, they are not publicly available. However, data may be obtained from the corresponding author on reasonable request and with permission from C.A.V.
